metrics.name: Resting Heart Rate

spaceflightShift.explanation: Microgravity removes the 2-meter hydrostatic hydrostatic pressure column on Earth, initially reducing cardiac sympathetic tone and resulting in a 4-8 bpm lower baseline in trained astronauts.

metrics.whatItIs: The frequency of myocardial contractions during complete physical rest, reflecting autonomic nervous system tone and cardiovascular conditioning.
metrics.whyItMatters: Elevated resting HR in space indicates autonomic exhaustion, cardiac deconditioning, acute infection, or excessive cumulative fatigue.

onboardMeasurement.device: Bio-Monitor Smart Shirt or Continuous Blood Pressure Device (CBPD) sensor patch
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Remain seated or tethered in sleep station for 5 minutes. Breathe regularly without speaking while sensor records 120-second resting baseline.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Drift > 12 bpm above personal baseline for 3 consecutive days, or resting HR > 105 bpm without exertion.
metrics.source: NASA-STD-3001, Vol 1, Rev B; Charles JB et al., Cardiovascular physiology in microgravity

metrics.name: Systolic Blood Pressure

spaceflightShift.explanation: Loss of gravitational pooling reduces lower-body blood pooling and alters central baroreceptor setpoint.

metrics.whatItIs: Peak pressure exerted against systemic arterial walls during ventricular systole.
metrics.whyItMatters: Hypotension increases risk of syncopal episodes in microgravity and during G-transitions; hypertension accelerates SANS optic disc edema.

onboardMeasurement.device: Continuous Blood Pressure Device (CBPD) finger cuff / oscillometric arm cuff
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Apply pneumatic cuff to upper left arm at heart level. Calibrate zero-point with finger sensor, sit relaxed for 3 deflation cycles.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Systolic BP > 145 mmHg or < 85 mmHg with orthostatic dizziness.
metrics.source: NASA-STD-3001, Vol 1; Norsk P., Blood Pressure Regulation in Space, Front Physiol 2020

metrics.name: Diastolic Blood Pressure

spaceflightShift.explanation: Peripheral vascular resistance declines slightly as vascular smooth muscle adapts to constant non-gravitational flow.

metrics.whatItIs: Minimum arterial pressure during ventricular diastole and cardiac refilling.
metrics.whyItMatters: Reflects systemic vascular resistance; sustained elevations impair cerebral autoregulation.

onboardMeasurement.device: Oscillometric arm cuff or CBPD continuous sensor
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Measured concurrently during automated systolic cuff inflation cycle.

metrics.name: Core Body Temperature

spaceflightShift.explanation: Spaceflight Space Fever phenomenon: Reduced evaporative convective cooling in closed air currents and inflammatory vascular response raises resting core temperature by approximately 0.5-1.0°C.

metrics.whatItIs: Deep visceral internal temperature measured through tympanic or infrared temporal artery sensors.
metrics.whyItMatters: Hyperthermia degrades cognitive performance and increases metabolic expenditure; rapid elevations indicate systemic infection.

onboardMeasurement.device: Double-sensor forehead heat-flux thermometer or tympanic IR probe
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Place dual-sensor patch flush against forehead midpoint or insert sanitized tympanic probe into auditory canal.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Core temp > 38.2°C (>100.8°F) or rapid drift > 1.2°C above personal baseline within 12 hours.
metrics.source: Stahn AC et al., Increased core body temperature in astronauts ('Space Fever'), Scientific Reports 2017

metrics.name: Fasting Blood Glucose

spaceflightShift.explanation: Microgravity induces insulin resistance due to physical inactivity of postural muscle groups and cortisol stress fluctuations.

metrics.whatItIs: Serum glucose concentration following an overnight fast or standardized caloric intake.
metrics.whyItMatters: Elevated glucose indicates metabolic dysregulation and glycation risks; hypoglycemia causes acute disorientation and tremor.

onboardMeasurement.device: Onboard Point-of-Care Capillary Glucometer or Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM)
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Cleanse fingertip with alcohol pad, activate sterile lancet, apply micro-droplet to test strip loaded in cartridge reader.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Fasting glucose > 145 mg/dL or < 65 mg/dL with adrenergic symptoms.
metrics.source: NASA Twins Study (Garrett-Bakelman et al., Science 2019); NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1

metrics.name: Sleep Duration

spaceflightShift.explanation: Astronauts historically average 6.0-6.4 hours of sleep per 24-hour cycle due to circadian disruption, noise, and sleep cabin micro-movements.

metrics.whatItIs: Total objectively recorded sleep time per 24-hour crew circadian rest period.
metrics.whyItMatters: Cumulative sleep debt impairs operational vigilance, slows reaction time, and triggers psychiatric instability.

onboardMeasurement.device: Actiwatch Sleep Logger & Smart Bio-Mattress Sensor
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Wear tri-axial actigraphy wrist unit continuous across sleep period; log subjective sleep onset/offset in morning check-in.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Cumulative sleep debt > 8 hours over rolling 5-day window, or single sleep period < 4.5 hours.
metrics.source: Barger LK et al., Prevalence of sleep deficiency in astronauts, Lancet Neurology 2014; NASA-STD-3001

metrics.name: Sleep Efficiency

spaceflightShift.explanation: Microgravity eliminates mattress contact pressure points; micro-awakenings are frequent from air current fluctuations and tether adjustments.

metrics.whatItIs: Percentage of total time in bed spent in actual restorative sleep (Stage N2, N3 slow-wave, and REM).
metrics.whyItMatters: Low sleep efficiency indicates restless sleep, REM fragmentation, and failure of cognitive recovery.

onboardMeasurement.device: Actigraphy sensor algorithm cross-referenced with EEG headband (Dreem/SleepView)
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Headband electrode array automatically syncs sleep architecture stages to HELIX upon waking.

metrics.source: NASA HRP BHP Sleep Architecture Findings; Dijk DJ et al., Sleep and circadian rhythms in spaceflight

metrics.name: Oxygen Saturation (SpO2)

spaceflightShift.explanation: Habitat ECLSS maintains nominal 21% O2 at 101.3 kPa (or 30% O2 at 56 kPa in exploration atmospheres), so SpO2 should remain normoxic.

metrics.whatItIs: Percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin relative to total hemoglobin in arterial blood.
metrics.whyItMatters: Drops indicate ECLSS partial pressure failure, smoke/trace contaminant inhalation, or pulmonary edema.

onboardMeasurement.device: Transmittance Pulse Oximeter finger probe or optical wrist sensor
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Attach sensor to index finger, rest arm, record stable plethysmographic waveform for 30 seconds.

metrics.escalationCriteria: SpO2 < 93% on ambient air without rapid recovery.
metrics.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2: ECLSS Normative Gas Partial Pressures

metrics.name: Body Mass

spaceflightShift.explanation: Immediate 2-3 kg fluid loss occurs within initial 72 hours due to cephalad shift and natriuretic diuresis; subsequent slow loss reflects caloric deficit and muscle atrophy.

metrics.whatItIs: Physical inertial mass of the astronaut measured via linear acceleration physics.
metrics.whyItMatters: Unintended body mass loss > 5% indicates nutritional deficit, bone/muscle breakdown, or inadequate hydration.

onboardMeasurement.device: Space Linear Acceleration Mass Measurement Device (SLAMD)
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Attach chest harness to SLAMD spring arm. Release catch and remain completely rigid while device measures oscillation frequency ($T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$).

metrics.escalationCriteria: Loss of > 4.0 kg from baseline within 14 days, or progressive continuous downward slope.
metrics.source: NASA HRP Nutrition and Physiology Evidence Book; Thornton WE., SLAMD calibration standards

metrics.name: Cumulative Radiation Exposure

spaceflightShift.explanation: Deep space transit vehicles receive ~1.5 mSv/day from Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR), reaching ~270 mSv over a 180-day transit.

metrics.whatItIs: Total career mission absorbed equivalent radiation dose in millisieverts.
metrics.whyItMatters: Permissible Career Limits (NASA standard: 600 mSv universal career limit for 3% Risk of Exposure-Induced Death from cancer).

onboardMeasurement.device: Personal Active Radiation Dosimeter (CPDS / Crew Passive Dosimeter badge)
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Insert personal dosimeter into optical docking bay on telemetry console for digital read-out sync.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Cumulative dose approaching 450 mSv or daily rate spike > 15 mSv/day (indicates active Solar Particle Event).
metrics.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1: Radiation Permissible Exposure Limits (PEL); NCRP Report No. 153

metrics.name: Daily Radiation Dose Rate

spaceflightShift.explanation: Baseline GCR rate in interplanetary transit is 1.2-1.8 mSv/day depending on solar cycle modulation.

metrics.whatItIs: Instantaneous rate of ionizing radiation absorbed over a 24-hour period.
metrics.whyItMatters: Acute spikes indicate a Solar Particle Event (SPE) coronal mass ejection requiring emergency storm shelter retreat.

onboardMeasurement.device: Vehicle Radiation Environment Monitor (VREM) / Silicon Solid-State Dosimeter
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Continuous autonomous telemetry broadcast synced to HELIX bus.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Rate > 5.0 mSv/day triggers AMBER alert; rate > 20 mSv/day triggers RED emergency storm shelter alarm.
metrics.source: NASA HRP Space Radiation Health Project Guidelines; Cucinotta FA et al.

metrics.name: Cognitive PVT Reaction Time

spaceflightShift.explanation: Initial spaceflight causes mild cognitive slowing (+15-25ms) due to neurovestibular adaptation and visual saccade adjustments.

metrics.whatItIs: Median visual response latency measured during a calibrated Psychomotor Vigilance Task test.
metrics.whyItMatters: Slowing reaction time directly correlates with operational error rate, docking failures, and cognitive micro-sleeps.

onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Focus on central visual counter. Press Spacebar or touch trigger immediately upon visual millisecond increment. 60-second duration.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Median reaction time > 320 ms or drift > 45 ms above personal baseline.
metrics.source: Basner M & Dinges DF., Psychomotor Vigilance Test in Operational Settings, Aerospace Med 2011; NASA HRP

metrics.name: PVT Attentional Lapses

spaceflightShift.explanation: Sleep fragmentation increases brief attentional state instability lapses (>500ms).

metrics.whatItIs: Number of reaction failures where response exceeded 500 milliseconds during a PVT session.
metrics.whyItMatters: Lapses indicate momentary neurobehavioral micro-sleeps where situational awareness is completely lost.
metrics.source: Dinges DF et al., Operational Fatigue and Vigilance Impairment, Sleep 1997

metrics.name: Mood & Emotional Valence

spaceflightShift.explanation: Third-quarter phenomenon: Long-duration crews typically experience lower emotional valence around midpoint of mission.

metrics.whatItIs: Self-reported emotional positivity and subjective affective state (1 = Severely Low, 5 = Highly Positive).
metrics.whyItMatters: Sustained dysphoria predicts crew conflict, withdrawal, and clinical depression in extreme isolation.

onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Select visual analog scale representing current emotional state upon waking.

metrics.source: Kanas N. et al., Behavioral issues with crewmembers in space, Aviat Space Environ Med 2009

metrics.name: Perceived Stress Level

spaceflightShift.explanation: High workload, tight mission timelines, and operational hazards create elevated background acute stress.

metrics.whatItIs: Subjective perception of cognitive overload and acute psychological tension (1 = Relaxed, 5 = Overwhelmed).
metrics.whyItMatters: Chronic stress accelerates cardiovascular dysregulation and suppresses cell-mediated immunity.

onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Rate mental tension and operational overwhelm during morning or evening log.

metrics.source: NASA HRP BHP Risk of Adverse Cognitive and Behavioral Conditions

metrics.name: Physical & Mental Fatigue

spaceflightShift.explanation: Constant exertion from 2.5h daily exercise plus sleep disruption creates baseline physical fatigue.

metrics.whatItIs: Subjective rating of physical exhaustion and lack of vital energy (1 = Energized, 5 = Exhausted).
metrics.whyItMatters: High fatigue increases musculoskeletal injury risk on ARED and reduces EVA safety margins.

onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Rate physical vitality upon completing daily operational schedule.

metrics.escalationCriteria: Fatigue >= 4.0 combined with PVT reaction time > 300 ms.
metrics.source: Samn-Perelli Fatigue Scale adapted for NASA Exploration Class missions

metrics.name: Countermeasure Exercise Compliance

spaceflightShift.explanation: NASA mission flight rules mandate 100% adherence to prescribed 2.5h daily exercise countermeasures (ARED + CEVIS).

metrics.whatItIs: Percentage of prescribed daily load-volume and aerobic duration completed on ARED and cycle ergometer.
metrics.whyItMatters: Skipping exercise causes rapid bone density loss (-1% per 30 days) and cardiovascular deconditioning.

onboardMeasurement.device: ARED (Advanced Resistive Exercise Device) Load Telemetry and CEVIS Wattmeter
onboardMeasurement.howToMeasure: Data stream logged automatically via Bluetooth/RS-422 telemetry from exercise console into HELIX.

metrics.source: NASA Flight Rule B13-105: Crew Countermeasure Exercise Requirements; NASA-STD-3001
